prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 250px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 168px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 105px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 1420px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A course-catalog comparison table: each row is one certified training course, and the reader picks a course by name, checks duration/trainer/fee, and reads the description only for shortlisted rows.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye enters at the right on the course name (the row identity), then moves left across duration and fee for quick comparison, treating trainer and description as supporting detail. Scanning is vertical down the name column and horizontal only between duration and fee.","groups":["col 1 (اسم الدورة) is the row header and anchor for every other column","col 2 (المدة) and col 5 (الرسوم) are the two short quantitative comparators and should read as a pair","col 3 (المدرب) and col 4 (الوصف) are supporting detail, read only after a row is shortlisted"],"keep_intact":["الرسوم values (short numbers, 43px word)","المدرب names (55px words) — personal names must not split","duration units and parentheticals (أيام / ساعة / بواقع)","Latin tokens inside names: Excel, PMP"],"may_wrap":["الوصف (1420px one-line) — the only genuinely long text, absorbs wrapping into 3–6 lines","اسم الدورة (250px) can take 2 lines without breaking identity","المدة (168px) can wrap the parenthetical onto a second line"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [120, 72, 56, 47, 64] · table 360×8323px · row heights [83, 1641, 1245, 1222, 1269, 1431, 1431] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 70 lines · mid-word splits 190
Design r0B: widths [230, 140, 95, 180, 70] · table 716×1324px · row heights [36, 246, 199, 199, 199, 222, 222] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 10 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 356px
Design r0C: widths [250, 168, 105, 400, 70] · table 994×650px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 83, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 634px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
